extracted.intended_audience: FFE State officials, Exchange operators, QHP issuers, state insurance regulators, and commenters on the proposed ACA rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory standards and reporting requirements for certifying non-network Qualified Health Plans (QHPs) and related criteria for FFE States to conduct Effective ECP/Provider Access Review Programs under the Affordable Care Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State ability to require QHP issuers to meet state ECP requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An FFE State must have the ability to require that QHP issuers continue to meet state ECP requirements and comply with ECP statutory requirements under section 1311(c)(1)(C) of the Affordable Care Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures ECP protections for low-income, medically underserved populations served by ECPs through plans where available; it is part of the processes that would allow an FFE State to be designated as having an Effective ECP Review Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for monitoring and addressing consumer-related complaints about ECP access
rubrics_metrics.description: §155.1051(e)(10) — FFE States must have a process for monitoring and addressing consumer-related complaints regarding access to ECPs to ensure sufficient access consistent with section 1311(c)(1)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important because access can change during the year (facility closures, network terminations, changes in services, funding or staffing shortages, directory inaccuracies, appointment availability, etc.). Demonstrates continuous monitoring and ability to ensure State ECP requirements have intended effect among consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, annual confirmation, and reevaluation of Effective ECP Review Program designation
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would notify an FFE State in writing prior to the start of the QHP certification cycle whether the FFE State is determined to have an Effective ECP Review Program; HHS would annually confirm whether the State wishes to continue conducting its own reviews and whether circumstances have changed that affect authority or technical capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS would reserve the right to evaluate an FFE State at any time and to determine it no longer satisfies criteria. HHS conducts annual environmental scans of state authorities to maintain situational awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of technical assistance and public ECP resources to FFE States
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would be available to provide technical assistance to FFE States on issues related to the Effective ECP Review Program and would continue to make ECP resources publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources include Final Plan Year ECP List, Rolling Draft ECP List, medical QHP and SADP ECP tools, Available ECP Write-in List, Plan Validation workspace in MPMS, and QHP certification website guidance. These resources aid identification of ECPs and assist issuers in meeting ECP requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection and standardization of ECP data from FFE issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would continue collecting ECP data from FFE issuers in FFE States with an Effective ECP Review Program to provide insight into issuer performance and to monitor consumer access across the FFE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collected data would be standardized and available to FFE States to inform ECP certification reviews and enable additional analyses across States; supports consistent issuer performance comparisons and complex ECP review work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network QHP must ensure access to providers accepting the plan's benefit amount as payment in full
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §156.236(a) — a non-network QHP must ensure access to a range of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full, including ECPs and providers that specialize in mental health and substance use disorder services, to ensure services will be accessible without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The set of providers willing to accept the benefit amount functions as the non-network plan's de facto 'network'; adequacy of that set determines whether the plan provides a sufficient choice of providers under sections 1311(c)(1)(B) and (C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report assessed percentage of available providers accepting benefit amount; ECP minimum percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(1) — the non-network plan must report its assessed percentage of available providers in each service area that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full; for ECPs, whether the plan meets at least a minimum percentage (as specified by HHS) of available ECPs that accept the benefit amount collectively across ECP categories and within certain individual ECP categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factor indicates how generous benefit amounts are and shows the issuer performed sufficient research/analysis to determine sufficient benefit amounts for an area; it gives Exchanges assurance enrollees can access providers who won't seek additional payment after plan payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: At least one ECP in each of the eight ECP categories per county
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(2) — whether the non-network plan offers the benefit amount as payment in full to at least one ECP in each of the eight ECP categories per county in the plan's service area (per §156.235(a)(2)(ii)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of plan's ability to cater to enrollee needs across priority health needs and socioeconomic factors; required to demonstrate compliance with section 1311(c)(1)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit amount offered to all available Indian health care providers in service area
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(3) — whether the non-network plan offers its benefit amount as payment in full to all available Indian health care providers in the plan's service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures Indian enrollees can receive applicable cost-sharing reductions without additional out-of-pocket costs; Indian providers are among those described under section 340B(a)(4) of the PHS Act and must be demonstrated for ECP access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy for continuous outreach to providers (including ECPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(4) — the non-network plan must report its strategy for conducting continuous outreach to available providers (including ECPs) to determine whether they would accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers not under contract are a moving target and may change charges; continuous outreach is imperative so plans can adjust benefit amounts to ensure enrollees can access a sufficient number of providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy for making benefit amounts publicly available in accessible format
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(5) — the non-network plan must report its strategy for making benefit amounts available to the public (enrollees, potential enrollees, and providers) in an easily accessible and understandable format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public availability signals to providers their charges may be too high and facilitates consumer shopping; transparency between plan, enrollee, and provider is crucial for non-network plans to function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for determining benefit amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(6) — the non-network plan must report its methodology for determining benefit amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows benefit amounts are not arbitrary but informed by analyses and research so amounts reasonably cover costs associated with services; example methodologies include percentage of benchmark, reference-based pricing, Medicare/private payor rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy for providing consumer-friendly information on balance billing and out-of-pocket costs
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(7) — the non-network plan must report its strategy for providing consumer-friendly and public information about potential balance billing scenarios and expected out-of-pocket costs, including historical data on actual out-of-pocket costs incurred by enrollees while accessing providers (including ECPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important because non-network plan design may be unintuitive and enrollees need education on how to use plans to limit unexpected costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions process for enrollees who cannot find providers accepting benefit amount
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(8) — report availability of an exceptions process under the non-network program for enrollees who cannot find providers (including ECPs) willing to accept the benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes circumstances where plan cannot protect consumers against out-of-pocket costs; an exceptions process could shift unavoidable additional out-of-pocket cost burden from the enrollee to the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer service and online provider directory assistance strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.236(b)(9) — the non-network plan must report its strategy for providing adequate customer service or online provider directory assistance to help enrollees and potential enrollees find providers (including ECPs) who will accept the benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures plan can assist enrollees in locating providers willing to accept benefit amounts and supports enrollee ability to shop and negotiate effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plans must meet general QHP certification criteria and benefit design standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposal, non-network plans would be subject to and allowed to demonstrate that they meet all general certification criteria at §155.1000(c), including minimum certification requirements in subpart C of part 156 and the requirement to comply with benefit design standards defined in §156.20 (EHB package).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a non-network plan does not exempt an issuer from general certification requirements; Exchanges must be satisfied non-network plans meet statutory QHP certification criteria to be certified.
